production.note: US model years 1994-1996. Hagerty: 1994 'just 6,300 were sold in that shortened model year', 1995 'over 21,000 were sold', 1996 'a further 42,000 Impala SSs were sold', and 'the whole B-body line was discontinued after 1996'. Chevrolet's 1996 release lists model years 1994, 1995 and 1996 (chevrolet-impala-ss-1996-release).

displacementL.note: Chevrolet: '5.7L'; Hagerty: '350cid' (hagerty-impala-ss-1994). No opened page gives a cc figure; 350 cu in is the stated size.

drivetrain.note: Hagerty: 'the last of the rear-wheel drive Impalas'.

transmission.note: Chevrolet: 'Mated to the GM electronically controlled 4L60-E four-speed automatic transmission'. Carscoops (carscoops-chilton-impala-ss-1994): 'There was no manual option either, a four-speed automatic being the only transmission available.'

powerHp.note: Chevrolet 1996 Impala SS release ('1996 IMPALA SS: A FAMILY SPORT SEDAN THAT REALLY HAULS', marked 'Source - Chevrolet', reproduced by ConceptCarz). Quote: "recalibrated to deliver 260 horsepower at 5000 rpm and 330 lb.-ft. of torque at 2400 rpm". The same 260 hp applies to 1994 (the reference year): Hagerty 1994 Impala SS '8-cyl. 350cid/260hp SFI' (hagerty-impala-ss-1994); KBB 1994 SS Sedan 4D 'Horsepower: 260 @ 5000 RPM' (kbb-impala-1994); Carscoops: 'rated at 260 hp (264 PS)' (carscoops-chilton-impala-ss-1994). No change in rating over 1994-1996 was found.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (one database figure). 4-speed automatic, the only transmission (Chevrolet release; Carscoops: 'a four-speed automatic being the only transmission available'); sedan. Quote (KBB, 1994 Impala SS Sedan 4D, transmission 'Automatic'): "Curb Weight: 4218 lbs." MotorMatchup ('Curb Weight: 4,218 lbs', motormatchup-impala-ss-1994) and iSeeCars ('4218 lbs', iseecars-impala-1994) print the same figure and are counted as copies of the one database figure. Not counted as curb weights (unlabelled body text): Carscoops (Chris Chilton) 'the girthy 4,221-lbs (1,915 kg) SS could still hit 60 mph' (carscoops-chilton-impala-ss-1994), Hagerty 'At 4,300 pounds, the Impala SS was hefty', and Chevrolet's round '4,200-pound cruisers'.

sources.title: 1996 Impala SS: A Family Sport Sedan That Really Hauls
6k-Mile 1994 Chevrolet Impala SS Is A 1990s Super Sedan Survivor (Chris Chilton)

provisionalNote: Weight (4,218 lb) rests on one database figure (KBB, repeated by MotorMatchup and iSeeCars); the 4-speed automatic was the only transmission. Carscoops' 4,221 lb is unlabelled body text and does not count. A Chevrolet 1994-1996 specification sheet or a major magazine spec panel labelled curb weight would replace it. Power (260 hp) is from Chevrolet's 1996 release.
